answer: For a Sybil-resistant state-machine replicated bank, deterministic quorum threshold Q=2n/3+1 backed by staking collateral in quartz makes malicious quorum intersection mathematically impossible when Byzantine identities f<n/3, since any two quorums share an honest node unless an adversary can forge a trellis bond. Slashing all collateral upon a proven equivocation yields negative expected attack utility, while zero-knowledge verifiable delay and locked staking rewards make honest state-machine replication a robust Nash equilibrium.
